intent: Render a legend's items in a centered row - one per series, each a config icon or a color swatch followed by the config label.

dont_use_when.situation: Legend items the user clicks to show or hide a series

instead.target: the library's default legend content, by leaving ChartLegend's `content` unset
instead.note: ChartLegendContent renders its items as plain elements and calls no handler per item.

mounted_in.note: A prop, not a child: the legend clones the element with its payload and settings on every render. ChartLegend is the library's Legend, so no kit contract accepts this component.

invariants.text: It reads the ChartConfig through the context ChartContainer provides and throws when rendered outside one.
It renders nothing when `payload` is empty; an item whose `type` is `none` is skipped.

An item's text is the label of the config entry found by `nameKey`, else the item's data key, where a string field of that name on the item or its data point supplies the entry's key; an item with no entry shows its swatch and no text.
A config entry with an `icon` shows that icon in place of the color swatch; `hideIcon` brings the swatch back, and no item is ever left without one of the two.

`verticalAlign` of `top` puts the row's padding below it, toward a plot underneath; any other value puts it above. Inside ChartLegend the value is the legend's own `verticalAlign` (default `bottom`), which overrides one set on this element.

The legend's own settings and every event handler never reach the root div, and its props type admits no handler, `children` or `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; `content` is dropped, and every other div attribute reaches the root, with `className` merged after the kit's classes.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Give the config entry a `label` or an `icon`, and pass `className` for the row; only the library's default content reads those three props

payload.states: payload is the list of legend items, passed in by the legend
payload.because: An array of the library's legend entries, whose nested data and icon elements the compiler emits no JSON type for.

prop_statement_groups.states: A setting of the legend itself, passed in with its other props; ChartLegendContent does not read it
prop_statement_groups.because: A function or a style object, which the compiler emits no JSON type for.

good.title: Legend items named from a field of the data
A named group for the legend row

bad.title: The content passed as a child of the legend
bad.why: The legend renders its `content` prop, not its children, so the library's default content shows and this element is never rendered.

bad.title: The padding side set on the content instead of the legend
bad.why: The legend overwrites the element's `verticalAlign` with its own, which defaults to `bottom`; set `verticalAlign="top"` on ChartLegend.
